videos.title: Measuring flour
recap: Stir the flour in the bag to loosen it.
Spoon it into the dry measuring cup until it's heaped.
Sweep the top flat with the back of a knife.
Never scoop the cup straight into the bag; it packs in extra flour.

videos.title: What the batter should look like
recap: Stir wet into dry just until no dry flour shows, about 10–15 strokes.
Lumps are good. Stop stirring.
After 5 minutes of rest it looks thicker and a little bubbly.

videos.title: When to flip
recap: Bubbles on top pop and leave holes that stay open.
The edges look dry and matte instead of shiny.
Usually 2–3 minutes on medium heat. Flip once.

videos.title: Soft scrambled eggs
recap: Medium-low heat; butter should foam gently, not brown.
Wait 20 seconds, then slowly push the eggs from the edge to the center.
Take them off the heat while they still look a little wet and glossy.

videos.title: How to roll a burrito
recap: Warm the tortilla first so it doesn't crack.
Filling in a line just below the middle.
Fold the bottom up, fold in both sides, then roll away from you, tucking as you go.

videos.title: Making a vinaigrette
recap: Shake the vinegar and salt first so the salt dissolves.
Add the mustard and oil.
Shake hard 20–30 seconds until cloudy and slightly thick.
Taste on a lettuce leaf, not a spoon.

videos.title: The pinch grip
recap: Pinch the blade just in front of the handle between your thumb and the side of your bent index finger.
Wrap your other three fingers around the handle.
Rock the knife forward and down; let the blade do the work.

videos.title: The claw grip
recap: Curl your fingertips under, like holding a ball.
Rest your knuckles against the side of the blade; they guide it.
Fingertips stay tucked behind your knuckles where the blade can't reach.

videos.title: Honing a knife
recap: Hold the steel upright with the tip resting on a towel.
Draw the blade down the steel at a slight angle, heel to tip.
Alternate sides, 5–6 strokes each. Honing straightens the edge; it doesn't sharpen.

videos.title: Dicing an onion
recap: Cut in half through the root and peel. Keep the root on; it holds the layers together.
Lay flat. Make lengthwise cuts up to, not through, the root.
Slice across those cuts with the claw grip. Toss the root end.

videos.title: Peeling and smashing garlic
recap: Lay the clove under the flat of your knife and press down with your palm.
The skin cracks and slips right off.
Press harder to smash it open. Smashed garlic gives the mildest, sweetest flavor.

videos.title: Slicing a bell pepper
recap: Cut off the top and bottom.
Slice down one side and unroll it into a flat sheet.
Trim away the white ribs, then slice into strips, skin side down.

videos.title: Against the grain
recap: Look for the lines running through the meat. Those are the muscle fibers.
Turn the meat so your knife crosses those lines.
Short fibers chew tender; long ones chew tough.

videos.title: Dicing a tomato
recap: Cut in half top to bottom and scoop out the watery seeds.
Lay flat and slice into ¼-inch strips.
Turn and cut across the strips into small dice.

videos.title: Cutting an avocado safely
recap: Never hold it in your hand. Lay it on the board, fingers on top.
Cut lengthwise all the way around the pit, then twist the halves apart.
Scoop out the pit with a spoon, then scoop the flesh.

videos.title: Slicing garlic
recap: Peel the clove and hold it with the claw grip.
Slice as thin as you can, about the thickness of a coin.
Keep slices even so they all turn golden at the same time.

videos.title: Golden vs burnt garlic
recap: Start garlic in cold oil over medium-low heat.
Golden and smelling sweet and nutty: done. Pull it now.
Brown and bitter-smelling: too far. Start over; it will taste bitter.

videos.title: Shredding cabbage
recap: Cut through the core into quarters, then cut out the hard core at an angle.
Lay a quarter flat side down.
Slice across as thin as you can.

videos.title: Julienne
recap: Cut into 3-inch lengths and slice lengthwise into thin planks.
Stack the planks.
Slice into thin matchsticks, about ⅛ inch.

videos.title: Gray vs. brown (Maillard)
recap: Pat meat completely dry; water makes it steam.
Hot pan, oil shimmering, pieces not touching.
Lay it down and don't touch it. It releases on its own when the crust forms.

videos.title: Boil vs. simmer
used_in: Boiled Pasta with Butter and Parmesan
recap: Rolling boil: big bubbles that keep going when you stir. For pasta and blanching.
Simmer: small, steady bubbles. For soups and sauces.
Bare simmer: a bubble or two every second. For stock and beans.

videos.title: Deglazing
recap: The brown bits stuck to the pan are flavor, not burnt food.
Pour liquid into the hot pan.
Scrape hard with a flat wooden spoon until the bottom comes clean.

videos.title: Folding an omelet
recap: As the bottom sets, lift an edge and tilt so runny egg flows under.
When the top is almost set, add filling to one half.
Fold the empty half over and slide it onto the plate.

videos.title: Al dente
used_in: Boiled Pasta with Butter and Parmesan
recap: Start tasting 2 minutes before the package time.
Bite a piece: cooked through but slightly firm in the very center.
No chalky white dot, not soft and limp.

videos.title: Cutting broccoli and squash
recap: Broccoli: cut florets off the stalk, then halve big ones into bite-sized pieces.
Squash: cut off both ends, peel, halve, scoop the seeds, then cube.
Same size pieces cook in the same time.

videos.title: Crowded vs spaced
recap: Crowded vegetables trap steam and turn soggy.
Spread in a single layer with space between pieces.
Use a second pan if they won't fit.

videos.title: The smash
recap: Pan very hot, cold beef ball in the pan.
Parchment on top, press down hard until ¼ inch thin.
Smash once, in the first 30 seconds, then leave it alone 1½–2 minutes.

videos.title: Mincing garlic
recap: Peel, then roughly chop.
Rock the knife back and forth over the pile, gathering it as you go.
Pieces smaller than a grain of rice. Minced garlic is sharp and burns fast.

videos.title: Blanching
recap: Boil in salted water just until bright green, 2–3 minutes.
Move straight into ice water to stop the cooking.
Drain and dry before sautéing.

videos.title: Where to put the thermometer
recap: Push into the thickest part of the meat.
Don't touch bone or the pan.
Whole chicken: thigh 175°F, breast at least 160°F (rises to 165°F as it rests).

videos.title: Carving a chicken
recap: Rest 15 minutes first.
Cut through the skin between leg and body, pull the leg out, cut through the joint.
Cut along the breastbone, following the bone down to lift off each breast. Slice across.

videos.title: Browning in batches
recap: Only one-third of the meat in the pot at a time, pieces not touching.
Leave it 3 minutes before turning.
Crowding makes it release water, steam and turn gray.

videos.title: Slicing onions without crying
recap: Use a sharp knife; dull blades crush more and release more of the sting.
Chill the onion 15 minutes first.
Halve through the root, peel, slice root to tip.

videos.title: Caramelized onion stages
recap: Pale and wilted after 10 minutes covered.
Soft gold, then peanut butter, then deep mahogany over 45–60 minutes on medium-low.
Add a splash of water when brown film builds up, and scrape.

videos.title: The risotto rhythm
recap: Keep the stock warm on a back burner.
Add one ladle at a time; stir until mostly absorbed.
Done when tender with a little bite, and loose enough to spread like a slow wave.

videos.title: Blooming spices
recap: Add ground spices to the hot oil and vegetables.
Stir constantly for about 30 seconds until strongly fragrant.
Add liquid right away; spices burn fast.

videos.title: Thickening with potatoes
recap: Simmer until a cube smashes easily against the pot.
Mash about half right in the pot.
Their starch turns the broth thick and creamy.

videos.title: Pan sauce
recap: Pour off all but a spoonful of fat; keep the brown bits.
Shallot 1 minute, then deglaze with about 1 cup liquid and scrape.
Reduce by half. Off the heat, swirl in cold butter.

videos.title: Roux stages
recap: White: 2–3 minutes, pale like wet sand, no raw-flour smell.
Blond: 5–7 minutes, light gold, smells like pie crust.
Brown: 15–20 minutes on medium-low, peanut-butter colored, nutty.
Dark specks or a burnt smell means start over.

videos.title: How thick is thick enough
recap: Dip a spoon in the sauce and turn it over.
Draw a line through the sauce with your finger.
If the line stays clean, it's thick enough. If it floods back, simmer longer.

videos.title: Grating garlic
recap: Rub a peeled clove across a microplane.
You'll get a smooth paste with no chunks.
Grated is the strongest form of garlic and burns in seconds. Cook it 30 seconds at most.

videos.title: Topping a pot pie
recap: Lay the crust over the thick filling.
Fold the edge under and press it to the rim. Brush with egg wash.
Cut 4 slits so steam can escape.

videos.title: Browning mushrooms
recap: Single layer, no salt yet, don't stir for 3–4 minutes.
They release water first; let it cook off.
Once they're golden, stir and salt.

videos.title: Mixing meatballs
recap: Soak breadcrumbs in milk first; this keeps them tender.
Mix with your hands just until combined, about 30 seconds.
Wet hands, roll golf-ball sizes. Cook to 160°F.

videos.title: Making cutlets
recap: Lay the breast flat, hand on top, and slice in half horizontally.
Between plastic wrap, pound to an even ½ inch.
Even thickness cooks through before the coating burns.

videos.title: The breading station
recap: Three dishes, left to right: flour, beaten egg, crumbs.
One hand for dry, one hand for wet.
Rest breaded pieces 10 minutes so the coating sticks.

videos.title: Basting a steak
recap: After both sides are seared, lower to medium.
Add butter, garlic and herbs. Tilt the pan so the butter pools.
Spoon the foaming butter over the steak for 1–2 minutes.

videos.title: Rinsing rice
recap: Rice in a fine-mesh strainer under cold water.
Swirl with your fingers about 1 minute.
Rinse until the water runs mostly clear. It keeps rice from turning gummy.

videos.title: Why cold water
recap: Potatoes go into cold salted water, then come to a boil together.
Hot water cooks the outside to mush before the center is done.
Done when a knife slides in with no resistance.

videos.title: Roughing up potatoes
recap: Parboil until the outsides are soft but centers firm.
Drain, add oil, lid on, shake hard 10–15 seconds.
The fuzzy outsides roast into a crunchy crust.

videos.title: Browning ground beef
recap: Hot pan, press the beef flat into one layer.
Leave it alone 4–5 minutes until the bottom is deep brown.
Then break it up and flip. Stirring right away turns it gray.

videos.title: Blending hot soup safely
recap: Immersion blender: keep the blade fully under the surface.
Regular blender: fill only halfway.
Remove the lid's center cap, cover the hole with a folded towel, hold the lid, start on low.

videos.title: Cutting in butter
recap: Freeze the butter 15 minutes.
Grate it on the large holes straight into the flour.
Toss with your fingertips to coat. Work fast; warm butter means flat biscuits.

videos.title: Folding biscuit dough
recap: Pat the dough into a 1-inch-thick rectangle.
Fold in thirds like a letter, turn, pat out again.
Three folds total, then cut straight down without twisting.

videos.title: What risen dough looks like
recap: More than doubled in size.
Surface dotted with bubbles.
Jiggles when you shake the bowl.

videos.title: What creamed butter looks like
recap: Softened butter and sugar beaten 2–3 minutes.
Paler in color and fluffy, like frosting.
Greasy and shiny means the butter was too warm.

videos.title: When to pull cookies
recap: Edges golden.
Centers still look pale and a little underdone.
They finish setting on the hot pan for 5 minutes.

videos.title: Melting chocolate
recap: Microwave 30 seconds at a time, stirring between each.
Stop when almost melted; stir until smooth.
Never let a drop of water in; it turns chocolate grainy.

videos.title: Toothpick test
recap: Poke a toothpick into the center.
A few moist crumbs: done and fudgy.
Wet batter: more time. Totally clean: a bit overbaked.

videos.title: Making crumble topping
recap: Flour, oats, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt in a bowl.
Pinch cold butter cubes into it with your fingertips.
Stop at pea-sized clumps with a few bigger ones.
